analysis:
Documentation-only change to docs/architecture/inference.md (head ranges 25-171 added, 868-869 edited, base 721 removed). The patch excerpt is truncated, so only the visible head text of units 7 and 8 was examined. That text describes existing deadline, MTP, MiMo and Qwen4 behavior and does not itself change code.

No security regression is visible. The prose repeatedly says candidate paths are internal, unregistered, unqualified and expose no HTTP route (for example the Nemotron Super local bridge). It also keeps the existing fail-closed and retention stances: native completion faults retain owners, unaffordable candidates fall back, and kill switches are unchanged. The SSD prefix-cache references (prefix-cache.md, lines ~726-730, 779-781, 805-807) match T-041: there are no new at-rest fields, the sampler is not part of cache identity, and the TTL is unchanged. No documented change touches T-041 mitigations, the cacheSalt scope, the TTL or the HMAC naming.

The new Nemotron Super section (added lines 25-171) is mostly outside the supplied excerpts. It says text prefix reuse runs only when the owner has a checkpoint bank, and that client prompt-cache keys are rejected. That is consistent with T-041's rule that caller-supplied cache keys do not participate.

The threat model may need a later update if the Nemotron Super local path becomes routable, because it could add a new prefix-cache and media surface. The supplied evidence does not show that. The head-side hunk at 868-869 is a small template-render-check doc edit and has no security impact.

I saw no cross-file interactions requiring a finding. The remaining Nemotron Super patch lines were not available in these units.
